info.adastraplanets.globe: Right-click to spin the globe. Power it with redstone to make it constantly spin.
info.adastraplanets.huge_launch_pad: A 7x7 launch pad for the biggest rockets: they need it from Tier 8. Also takes every smaller rocket. Launches any rocket placed on its centre. Power with redstone to automatically launch placed rockets.
info.adastraplanets.large_launch_pad: A 5x5 launch pad for bigger rockets: they need it from Tier 6. Launches any rocket placed on its centre. Power with redstone to automatically launch placed rockets.
jei.adastraplanets.access_card: The lost expedition's card, left in their camps. Swipe it on an access reader to open the door beside it for good; the card is kept.
jei.adastraplanets.ancient_ship: Kept on the cradle in the Hangar of the ark behind the Last Door on Eris. It reaches any body and needs no fuel; it launches from an ordinary launch pad.
jei.adastraplanets.ancient_suit: Kept in the Arsenal of the ark behind the Last Door on Eris. Worn as a full set, in the armor slots or in the liner's Curios slots (or mixed), it needs no oxygen, liner or temperature protection.
jei.adastraplanets.core_socket: Found in the ancients' ruins and landmarks; it cannot be broken. A crystal socket takes its system's crystal shard, a core socket its system's Light Core. Once filled, it powers the gates and seals it touches.
jei.adastraplanets.light_core: A system's Light Core, kept at the end of its great landmark (use /locate structure with the landmark's id). The NASA Workbenches use one as a catalyst: it comes back out of the grid. Set all seven in the threshold of the Last Door on Eris to open it.
log.adastraplanets.door.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - ERIS
Entry 120

The door. Seven stones in its threshold, seven hollows the size of a fist, each ringed in a colour I have seen on a world behind me.
log.adastraplanets.door.0.1: I have none of the lights. I left every one where it lay, as Ilse asked. Somewhere under this plain the last of them sleeps in the ice; I went down once and came back with frost in my lungs.
log.adastraplanets.door.0.2:
So I wait. The sun is a star from here. Whoever you are, you carried them all this way: set them in their stones, nearest the sun first. Then go back to Pluto and wake her.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.forge.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - TRITON
Entry 97

Four chimneys and a stack breathing nitrogen, and under them a forge. The ancients worked metal here with the heat that drives Triton's geysers.
log.adastraplanets.forge.0.1: The vault's door is a slit of rune stone as tall as the hall, and its two sockets are up in the wall where no one can climb. Ilse watched the geysers in the floor below them for an hour, then laughed.
log.adastraplanets.forge.0.2:
Stand on the vent and wait. It throws you right up to the ledge. Past the door, the bridge breathes fire every few seconds: count, then run.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.heart.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - PLUTO
Entry 112

Ilse went down into the crypt three days ago to read the sleepers' names. She has not come back up. The seal at the bottom is shut again.
log.adastraplanets.heart.0.1: I set a stone for her by the ship, and one beside it I could not bring myself to name. I locked the bunker so nothing follows her down. The card is in the chest.
log.adastraplanets.heart.0.2:
I am taking the ship to the edge, to the last door, alone. If she wakes, she will know where I have gone.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.heart.1.0:
R.,

If you are reading this, you came down after all. They are not tombs. The sleepers are not dead. They are waiting for the lights to come home.
log.adastraplanets.heart.1.1: The seal took the reliquaries' light and closed behind me, and the reliquaries grew it back. The heart keeps its own.
log.adastraplanets.heart.1.2:
I am going to lie down with them. Go on to the door. Bring every light, all seven. Then come and wake me.

- Ilse
log.adastraplanets.library.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - TITAN
Entry 71

The haze lifted for an hour and there it was: a tower in a ring of methane, three stone rings round it like Saturn's own, as if the builders had wanted the planet to see itself.
log.adastraplanets.library.0.1: The door is sealed twice: two sockets, both wanting the pale crystal of this system. We have one from the geodes. Ilse swears she saw a second in a shrine on the lowest ring.
log.adastraplanets.library.0.2:
Inside, she says, it is a library, and the archive at the top is a lock made of words. Read everything. Touch only what the books tell you to.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.observatory.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - MIRANDA
Entry 84

A telescope. A stone telescope, sixty metres of it, leaning like the planet it watches. Uranus fills its lens.
log.adastraplanets.observatory.0.1: The mouth is sealed with four sockets, and each glows a different colour: the red of Phobos, the amber of Europa, the pale gold of Titan, and this system's own blue.
log.adastraplanets.observatory.0.2:
We carried samples of every one, thank Ilse. If you came after us without them, go back for them: the geodes keep growing.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - OUTPOST
Entry 41

The dig under the hangar broke into a hall that was here long before us. Black stone, cut like glass. Runes that glow when nobody touches them.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.0.1:
At its end, a door. No hinges, no lock we understand. Beside it, an empty socket the size of a fist.

Dr. Ilse thinks the door is waiting for something. 'The light of this world', the runes say, if Ilse reads them right.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.0.2:
We found red crystals in the geodes down in the grooves. Same red as the runes on the door.

Security sealed the passage until we know what we are dealing with. Access card required.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.1.0:
PERSONAL LOG - R.

Could not sleep again. The crew is tired of this rock and of me.

The commander's card is in her locker, top row, the one with the red tape. She says nobody goes down the passage without her.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.1.1:
Ilse put two of the red shards in the sample case in the lab. One went into her test socket and a little gate opened, just like that. The other is for the big door.

We are close.
log.adastraplanets.outpost.1.2:
If anyone reads this: the security line in the passage is still armed. Tripwires. Cut them with shears or crawl.

I am going down tonight.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.sanctuary.0.0:
EXPEDITION LOG - EUROPA
Entry 58

The signal Ilse decoded on Phobos points here, straight down through the ice. We set the rig on the brightest patch of the shell and started drilling.
log.adastraplanets.sanctuary.0.1:
Thirty-six metres of ice, then nothing: the drill broke into open water. An ocean, under the ice, and something in it shining amber.

We have built a bell at the bottom of the bore.
log.adastraplanets.sanctuary.0.2:
Ilse found one of the amber crystals in the cores we pulled up. She thinks the temple below has more than one lock this time.

The spare crystal is in the store cabin.

- R.
log.adastraplanets.sanctuary.1.0:
PERSONAL LOG - R.

The tube is done. Glass all the way down, past the temple's face and in under it. The water stops at the rim of the pool inside, as if the place expects visitors who breathe.
log.adastraplanets.sanctuary.1.1:
Two chapels, two sockets, one door that wants both. The trenches pull you down onto something hot. Swim hard or bridge them.

Take the potions. Do not trust your suit down there.

- R.
lore.adastraplanets.door.clue.0.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the Door]

Seven worlds, seven lights. Set each in its stone, from the nearest the sun to the farthest, and the way home opens.
lore.adastraplanets.door.clue.0.1: The last light sleeps under the ice of this world. Go down where the stair goes down, and follow only the light that is lit: the dark ways take the careless.
lore.adastraplanets.door.hangar.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the cradle]

Here rested the ship that needs no fire. It goes where the lights have gone, and comes back.
lore.adastraplanets.door.origin.0:
[Inscription of the Hall of Origin]

To the one who returned the lights: we were a people of a young sun, and we went outward, world by world, each colder than the last.
lore.adastraplanets.door.origin.1: On every world we raised a door and left a light in it, and on every world some of us stayed to keep it. They sleep still, by the heart, in the ice, under the seas.
lore.adastraplanets.door.origin.2: This ark was to carry the rest of us home. We never sailed it. The road was longer than our lives; the lights were scattered; the door would not open for so few.
lore.adastraplanets.door.origin.3: Now it is open. Take what we left: the garment that needs no air, and the ship that needs no fire. Then go to the heart of the far world and wake the sleepers. Tell them the lights came home.
lore.adastraplanets.heart.clue.0.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the gallery]

Here sleep those who stayed. The road of the living is stone; the snow is for the sleepers.
lore.adastraplanets.heart.clue.0.1: Two lights rest at the ends of the hall. Carry them to the heart's door, and walk only on stone.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.0.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the library]

Six keep watch over the archive. Only four may be called, and they answer only in the order of the sky.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.0.1:
First call the light that every world circles.

Then call what circles the lord of these moons.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.1.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the library]

The third is the sea that is not water, on the world that keeps this house.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.1.1: Do not wake the moon, nor the star. They sleep, and they bite.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.2.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the orrery]

Last, call the eye: the far moon, dark on one face and bright on the other, that watches from the edge.
lore.adastraplanets.library.clue.2.1: When four have answered, the stair to the sky will open.
lore.adastraplanets.observatory.clue.0.0:
[Expedition translation, inscription of the mount]

Who would look upon the far worlds must first have walked the near ones.
lore.adastraplanets.observatory.clue.0.1: Bring the light of every world you crossed. Set each where its colour shines. Then climb, and look.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.0.0:
[Expedition translation, fragment I]

We came from beyond the last light. On every world we raised a door, and in every door we left the light of that world.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.0.1: The light sleeps in the stone, deep, where the ice remembers. Whoever carries it back to the door may pass.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.0.2:
(In the margin, in a human hand:)

The socket wants the crystals from the geodes. Same colour as these runes. Don't step on the plates.

- R.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.1.0:
[Expedition translation, fragment II]

The sun was young when we left. We went outward, world by world, each colder than the last.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.1.1: What we kept, we sealed. What we lost, we wrote. Read the walls and follow the cold.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.1.2:
(In the margin:)

They went outward too, just like us. Where did they stop?

- R.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.2.0:
[Expedition translation, fragment III]

At the edge, where the farthest world turns slowly, we built the last door. Beyond it lies the way home.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.2.1: Do not open what the frost keeps. Not until every light is returned.
lore.adastraplanets.ruin.2.2:
(In the margin:)

Every light... one for each system? The crew thinks I'm obsessed. Maybe I am.

- R.
